source_refs.note: Topic 7.6.5.1 (PDF 190, printed 187). The printed list numbers its examples as items 2 and 4. Long question 5 is answered; contrast, captions and keyboard use are general knowledge, flagged.

items: Readable fonts: clear, large fonts such as Arial or Times New Roman instead of decorative styles.
Alternative text for images: describe images, charts and graphs so visually impaired users, who may use screen readers, can understand them.

blocks.prompt: Explain creating accessible digital content and strategies for inclusivity (long question 5).
blocks.explanation: Accessible content is designed from the start for all users. Strategies from the chapter: clear, large fonts and alternative text for images and charts. Further common practices: strong colour contrast, captions or transcripts for audio and video, headings and labels that screen readers can follow, content usable with a keyboard alone, and plain language. Asking users, including people with disabilities, for feedback shows what still needs fixing. The further practices are general knowledge.

items: Accessibility: readable fonts and alt text, plus contrast, captions and screen-reader-friendly structure.
